findings.text: job.sh and the six decision-record JSON files at docs/evidence/fragments/code-reuse-and-hot-path/hot-path-duplicates/ are delivered but not declared: with receipt.json and ast-scan.json they make seven of eleven paths outside the dispatch's write paths, so the declaration does not cover the delivery even though the node brief required the decision records; the register documents the gap at hot-path-duplicates.html:41-55 and the manifest records it under outside_scope.

the four candidate decisions under candidate-agreements.decisions carry id, question, options, recommended, keeper and lines_removable but omit the context, project, plan and section keys the node brief requires of a decision record, so recording them with crew decision record needs the coordinator to reconstruct the compared input, the route, and the plan/section identity from the register rather than from the record.

the cited 7-entry gate result was produced by an out-of-tree script (~/.cache/nova-s33/hpd-verify/gate_repair.sh, recorded in gate-repair.log) while the manifest's tests line names job.sh, whose only recorded log (compare.log) reports the earlier 6-entry run at 85d69cfc5; re-running job.sh at the head would reproduce seven entries because compare.py is byte-identical since 717375353, but no job.sh log at the head revision is recorded.

rubric.durability: answered: no suite test fails if the register, driver or decision records regress; the driver enforces its three negative controls and the definitions cross-check by exit status but is a standalone prototype not wired into any test lane, and the decision-record files are not checked by the gate.
rubric.evidence: answered: compare.py's gate result is recorded in gate-repair.log at revision 717375353 with EXIT=0 and reconciles with the committed receipt's seven entries and three negative controls; the named gate command's own log reports the earlier six-entry run.
rubric.fit: answered: descriptive file and symbol names, no plan or stage labels in source; the only sprint token is the mandated option value accept-for-s28-node in the decision records that the node brief specifies.
rubric.goal_fidelity: answered: the register, its six decision records, the measured four-candidate section and the driver together deliver plan section 5's record, with every entry naming implementations, route, tolerance, keeper and removable lines.
rubric.reuse: answered: compare.py loads scripts/iron_operator_bound/reuse_check.py and calls its definitions() for all 210 route modules, cross-checking its own body walk module by module; the body-digest and near-identity grouping it adds has no owner in reuse_check.py, whose only exports are definitions(), callers() and the four-owner scan.
rubric.scope_discipline: answered: seven of eleven delivered paths fall outside the declared write paths; all are merge-safe evidence or the gate runner inside the section's area and are enumerated in the register.
